Compare nested models with the same number of classes

compare_models.Rd

Likelihood-ratio tests of nested models with the same number of classes: the naive test and the Satorra-Bentler scaled difference test that Mplus uses with MLR. Typical uses: full against partial or no measurement invariance in a multigroup model or an LTA, or equal against free variances in an LPA.

Usage

compare_models(m0, m1, ...)

Arguments

m0, m1

Fitted latentmix models. m0 may also be a (possibly named) list of models, in which case m1 and ... are not used.

...

Further fitted models, for a comparison table.

Value

With two models, an object of class c("latentmix_compare", "latentmix_aux"): a list with ll0, ll1 (log-likelihoods), npar0, npar1 (free parameters), c0, c1 (scaling factors), df, chisq, p (naive test), cd, chisq_scaled, p_scaled (scaled test), delta_aic, delta_bic, delta_sabic (M1 minus M0), warning (empty string if none) and labels (labels of M0 and M1). With several models, a data frame of class c("latentmix_comparison", "data.frame") with one row per model (model (label), K, npar, ll, scaling, aic, bic, sabic, entropy, and, against the previous row, df, chisq, cd, chisq_scaled, p_scaled, warning; the tests are NA on the first row). Both print and work with lm_table().

Details

Two models. compare_models(m0, m1) tests the model with fewer free parameters against the other (the two are reordered by number of parameters if necessary; they must differ in it). The naive statistic is \(2(LL_1 - LL_0)\); the scaled statistic is \(TR_d = 2(LL_1 - LL_0)/c_d\) with \(c_d = (p_1 c_1 - p_0 c_0)/(p_1 - p_0)\), where \(p\) are the numbers of free parameters and \(c\) the MLR scaling factors (scaling_factor()), both on \(p_1 - p_0\) degrees of freedom. A warning is returned (component warning) when \(c_d \le 0\) or the numbers of classes differ. Nesting is not checked: it is the user's responsibility.

Several models (three or more, or a list): each model is tested against the previous one (in the direction of fewer to more parameters) and the result is a comparison table; consecutive models with the same number of parameters get no test.

The chi-square reference distribution does not apply to models with different numbers of classes; use lmr() or blrt() for those.

References

Satorra, A., & Bentler, P. M. (2001). A scaled difference chi-square test statistic for moment structure analysis. Psychometrika, 66(4), 507–514. doi:10.1007/BF02296192

See also

lrtest(), scaling_factor(), lmr(), blrt().

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# Measurement invariance of the ACE classes across sex (female: 0/1)
full <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female)
#> Starting Julia ...
part <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "ace_sex_abuse")
none <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "none")
compare_models(full, part)        # scaled chi-square: freeing ace_sex_abuse improves fit
#> ━━ Nested model comparison ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   full (M0) nested in part (M1)
#> 
#>   ──────────────────────────────────
#>   Model            LL  Par.  Scaling
#>   ──────────────────────────────────
#>   M0: full  -6285.709    39   1.0374
#>   M1: part  -6263.901    43   1.0381
#>   ──────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Difference tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Test                          Chi-square  df       p
#>   ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Likelihood ratio (naive, ML)      43.615   4  <0.001
#>   Satorra-Bentler scaled (MLR)      41.724   4  <0.001
#>   ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Scaling correction of the difference cd = 1.0453
#>   ΔAIC = -35.615, ΔBIC = -14.362, ΔsaBIC = -27.069 (M1 - M0)
compare_models(full, part, none)  # all three models; partial invariance is the true model
#> Nested model comparison
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Model  K  Par.         LL  Scaling        BIC  df  Chi-square      cd  Scaled chi-square  Scaled p
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> full   4    39  -6285.709   1.0374  12856.633   —           —       —                  —         —
#> part   4    43  -6263.901   1.0381  12842.271   4      43.615  1.0453             41.724    <0.001
#> none   4    71  -6248.025   1.0573  13015.290  28      31.751  1.0868             29.215     0.402
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Each model is tested against the previous one. Scaling = MLR scaling correction factor; cd = scaling correction of the difference; scaled test = Satorra-Bentler (Mplus MLR).
lm_table(compare_models(full, part), format = "markdown")
#> **Nested model comparison**
#> 
#> |  | LL | Par. | Scaling | Chi-square | df | p |
#> | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
#> | *Models* |  |  |  |  |  |  |
#> | M0: full | -6285.709 | 39 | 1.0374 |  |  |  |
#> | M1: part | -6263.901 | 43 | 1.0381 |  |  |  |
#> | *Difference tests* |  |  |  |  |  |  |
#> | Likelihood ratio (naive, ML) |  |  |  | 43.615 | 4 | <0.001 |
#> | Satorra-Bentler scaled (MLR) |  |  |  | 41.724 | 4 | <0.001 |
#> 
#> *cd = 1.0453 (scaling correction of the difference); ΔBIC (M1 - M0) = -14.362.*  
# }
